info.title: Integriq
info.description:
The JSON API of Integriq, the integration hub for Nextcloud: sources, endpoints, mappings, synchronisations, jobs and their logs, and the connectors to government and education standards (DSO, StUF, ZGW Notificaties, SCIM, LTI, OpenID4VCI, Peppol and others). The sources, mappings and other objects themselves are stored in OpenRegister and read and written through its API; this document covers the endpoints Integriq adds on top. Endpoints that implement an external protocol keep that protocol's error format.

Every path is served under `/api/v1/`, the version this document describes. The unversioned `/api/` paths keep working, are deprecated, and name their `/api/v1/` successor in a `Link` header next to a `Deprecation` header. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`), and every response carries an `API-Version` header. Paths that implement an external standard keep the formats of that standard and are not described here; where this app documents them, openapi.standards.json does.

post.summary: Link a source to a connection that has none, probe it, and return both
post.description: Link a source to a connection that has none, probe it, and return both.  Admin-only and CSRF-protected: a link decides which credentials a health probe calls with. The body carries either `source` (an existing source uuid) or `fromTemplate: true` (make or reuse the source named by the connection's `sourceTemplate`).

200.description: `{connection, probe}` on success; an `error` with 400, 404, 409 or 500 otherwise.

post.summary: Resolve a single value from a named source
post.description: Resolve a single value from a named source.  Authenticated NC user only (enforced by `#[NoAdminRequired]`'s implicit "logged-in user required", no `#[PublicPage]`). Honours the source's own read-authorization: a source the current user may not read yields 403, never a fetch. Any `url`/`host` in `params` is ignored, egress is always derived from the stored source, never the caller.

200.description: `{value, fetchedAt, stale}` on success; 400/403/404/500 with an `error` key otherwise.

get.description: Who owns the record behind this reference.  An object no synchronisation maintains answers `local` and the call succeeds. It is not an error to ask about a record nobody follows.  SCOPED TO THE CALLER, WITHOUT BREAKING THE UNKNOWN-ANSWERS-LOCAL CONTRACT.  The ownership answer names the synchronisation, the source id and when the record was last seen, facts about a record, not about the asker, and this used to answer for any id at all.  A 404 for an unreadable id would have contradicted the scenario this method is tagged with: an object nobody follows answers `local` and the call succeeds. So an id the caller cannot read answers `local` too. That is the same answer an unknown id gets, which is the point, the two are indistinguishable, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover that a record exists or who maintains it.

post.summary: Login a user based on username and password combination  This method securely authenticates a user using their username/
post.description: Login a user based on username and password combination  This method securely authenticates a user using their username/email and password, with comprehensive protection against XSS and brute force attacks including: - Input validation and sanitization - Rate limiting per user and IP - Progressive delays for repeated attempts - Account and IP lockout mechanisms - Security event logging - Security headers in response  RATE-LIMIT RATIONALE (ADR-082). A LOGIN endpoint, so much tighter than anything else in this app: this is the one public surface here where the caller presents a credential a stranger could guess.  Brute-force protection is ALREADY COMPLETE here, and deliberately not via NC's IThrottler: SecurityService::checkLoginRateLimit() gates entry (with a lockout and a delay), recordFailedLoginAttempt() feeds it on both failure paths, and recordSuccessfulLogin() clears it. That is the two-halves shape ADR-082 asks for, keyed on USERNAME + IP rather than IP alone, finer-grained than the framework throttler, so adding BruteForceProtection on top would be a second, coarser counter for the same event.  The AnonRateLimit ceiling below is the volume half, which app-local logic did not cover.

title.description: The HTTP reason phrase of the status.
